evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: This story creates the primary resource (a game) and does not inherently require any other backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators via a game URL inherently requires a game to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: start a round
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round is an action within a game and therefore depends on a game being created first.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the list of items is self-contained; it can be implemented and show an empty list without requiring another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item presumes items exist in the list, which depends on the ability to add items first.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item creates the resource and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item requires that an item already exists, which depends on the ability to add items.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item presumes items are present; it depends on functionality to create/add items first.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: This is a display/behavioral feature for estimate presentation and does not inherently require a different backlog story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average is a standalone decision/processing feature and does not inherently depend on another specific story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: This behavior can be implemented as part of the estimate-handling logic without requiring another specific backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering the agreed estimate is a standalone action and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating an earlier story inherently depends on the existence of prior rounds/items (ability to start rounds and have prior estimates).

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories is self-contained and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste import is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games presumes previous games exist, which depends on the ability to create games.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game's transcript requires that games and transcripts are generated/stored (i.e., games must exist).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript presumes a transcript exists and thus depends on transcript/viewing functionality.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: As with HTML export, CSV export requires a transcript to be available and therefore depends on transcript production/viewing.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game inherently requires that a game exists to be deleted (created earlier).

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is a primary action and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in requires an account to exist first (account creation).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details presumes an account already exists and thus depends on account creation.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account inherently requires that the account exists (created previously).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Displaying local timezone information is a standalone presentation feature and does not require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders require an existing account with an email address; thus this depends on account creation.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting the estimate scale is a configuration feature and does not inherently require another story.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators presumes an invitation mechanism and game context; this is a constrained form of the invite feature and depends on the invite functionality.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a received URL presumes that an invitation/game URL mechanism exists (invite functionality) and a game to join.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the current item requires a round/item to have been started/selected, which depends on round-starting or item-adding functionality.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the list of upcoming items is a self-contained view feature and can be implemented regardless of other specific backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This is a presentation/notification behavior about estimates and does not inherently depend on another single backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: This is a behavior for reveal timing and can be implemented without depending on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate before reveal is a standalone interaction rule and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates requires stored history of previous estimates/rounds; this depends on functionality to browse or store prior rounds/estimates.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Displaying current-round attribution is a presentation feature and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer feature is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Resetting the two-minute timer presumes the timer exists; it therefore depends on the timer feature story.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling prior rounds presumes prior rounds and stored estimates exist (i.e., round/start and storage must be implemented first).

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card-order consistency is a presentation/interaction rule that can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: This is an interaction rule for estimate changes and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail is a UI feature that does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a developer goal that is self-contained and not dependent on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing definitions is self-contained and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating indexes is a developer task that does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is a non-functional requirement that can be addressed independently.

evaluations.evidence: have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a standalone quality requirement and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is a cross-cutting non-functional requirement and not inherently dependent on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a platform capability that can be implemented without depending on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is an independent usability requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page design is a standalone feature and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Privacy/anonymization of stored results is a standalone requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Providing usage metrics is a feature that can be implemented independently (though it consumes data, it does not inherently require another single backlog story).
